key_insight: OmniShotCut reconceptualizes shot-boundary detection as structured relational prediction: a Shot-Query Transformer jointly models shot boundaries and inter-shot relations to produce more interpretable, sensitive, and robust boundary predictions.
problem_solved: Current SBD models produce hard-to-interpret boundaries, miss subtle but harmful discontinuities, and depend on noisy, low-diversity annotations and outdated benchmarks—OmniShotCut addresses these by modeling holistic shot relations and improving evaluation robustness.
method: Shot-Query Transformer: learnable shot queries attend to video features to directly predict shot boundaries and associated relational labels.
Holistic relational prediction: joint estimation of boundaries plus pairwise shot relations to disambiguate gradual vs. abrupt transitions and improve interpretability.
Improved evaluation: introduces a more robust benchmark/protocol (and/or data refinement) to better capture subtle discontinuities and reduce annotation noise.
impact: Gives practitioners more reliable and interpretable shot segmentation for downstream tasks (video indexing, editing, retrieval, and training robust video models) and raises the bar for SBD evaluation.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: Shot-Query Transformer flow (video frames → queries → boundary + relation outputs) with attention arrows.
Before/after timeline: video timeline with ground-truth vs. OmniShotCut boundaries color-coded (highlighting subtle/gradual transitions).
Attention/interpretability overlay: frame sequence with attention heatmaps showing why a boundary was predicted.
Benchmark comparison chart: precision/recall or F1 improvements across standard and new benchmarks.
paper_title: OmniShotCut: Holistic Relational Shot Boundary Detection with Shot-Query Transformer
paper_authors: Boyang Wang, Guangyi Xu, Zhipeng Tang, Jiahui Zhang, Zezhou Cheng
